summary: MARS GPS is a prototype Mars mission-planning dashboard designed to support astronaut surface exploration. It combines NASA Mars mapping-layer information with interactive route planning, grid-based pathfinding, terrain difficulty estimation, and hazard checks. Users can explore a simulated Martian environment, select destinations, and generate routes while considering potential obstacles. The project demonstrates how planetary data and navigation tools could help organize safer and more informed future Mars surface missions.
details: MARS GPS – Mars Mission Planner is a web-based prototype designed to demonstrate how astronauts could plan surface exploration routes on Mars. The project has two main components: 1. Frontend dashboard: Built with Python Flask, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It provides an interactive Mars exploration interface, a simulated terrain grid, rover controls, destination selection, and mission information. 2. Backend services: Built with Python FastAPI. It provides route estimation, route planning, terrain difficulty estimation, hazard checks, coordinate calculations, and science-point management. The frontend uses an A* pathfinding algorithm to calculate a route across a 10×10 demonstration grid while avoiding blocked cells. The backend also includes NASA Mars Trek WMTS layer and capabilities endpoints to retrieve information about available Mars map layers. The project aims to demonstrate how planetary mapping resources, navigation algorithms, and hazard-aware route planning could support future Mars exploration. Its current grid and hazard model are simulations and are not certified for real astronaut navigation. The project was developed using Python, Flask, FastAPI, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and GitHub.
